headline: ASX surges 1.4% to close near 8,900 as oil crashes 5.7% on Iran ceasefire hopes — big week ahead with Wednesday's CPI print set to shape the RBA's next move.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a strong session today, up 2.7% to $4.25. Lithium sentiment got a lift from broader commodity enthusiasm and some analyst attention today, though the stock remains well below its entry price. The long-term story hinges on the lithium market recovering — that thesis hasn't changed.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG had a solid session today, up 0.85% to $75.75, riding the ASX's strong 1.4% rally. As a diversified ETF across Australian and global shares, it broadly tracks the market's mood — and today's mood was positive.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE closed up 0.7% today to $92.07. The Aussie dollar also rose (now around 70 US cents), which can slightly dampen returns for an unhedged ETF holding overseas assets — but today's price action was still positive. Emerging markets sentiment has been cautiously improving.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS gained 0.55% today to close at $525.84. This ETF tracks the entire US share market, so it benefited from last night's broadly flat-to-positive US session. It's now in positive territory overall for the portfolio — a solid position.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 0.32% today to $15.51, continuing a slow grind. CNBC reported today that the AI boom is now lifting industrial stocks — not just tech — which is a broader tailwind for this ETF. The fund is still down on the overall investment, but the AI thematic remains very much intact.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO rose 0.61% last night to $231.65, nearly breaking even on the overall position (just $1.49 in the red). No specific news catalyst — the stock is just quietly ticking up. GTA VI remains the long-term catalyst to watch.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG edged up 0.24% last night to $319.09 after a strong Q2 earnings report — Alphabet posted $119.8B in revenue for the quarter. The stock has had a solid run and the Motley Fool noted it looks attractive after earnings. Google also raised Pixel device prices, signalling confidence in the premium hardware space.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT was essentially flat last night, up just 0.03% to $381.70. All eyes are on Microsoft's earnings report this week — it's still about 30% off its all-time high and the market is waiting for proof that its massive AI investment is paying off. Earnings could be a big catalyst in either direction.

watch_today.title: MSFT earnings this week — the big test
watch_today.detail: Microsoft reports earnings this week (US time). The stock is still ~30% off its highs and investors need to see that its huge AI spending is actually driving revenue growth. This could move the stock significantly — worth watching closely. As a long-term holder, don't overreact to a single quarter, but if the numbers disappoint badly, be aware.

watch_today.title: Wednesday CPI print — critical for RBA interest rate decision
watch_today.detail: Australia's June quarter inflation data drops Wednesday morning. This is essentially the deciding factor for whether the RBA cuts, holds, or (worst case) hikes rates at its next meeting. A higher-than-expected number could spook markets and put pressure on rate-sensitive holdings. Keep an eye on this — it affects the whole portfolio.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — good day but still deeply underwater
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals bounced 2.7% today to $4.25, which is encouraging. But the position is still down nearly 37% overall. The lithium price recovery is the key — until there are clearer signs of a sustained rebound in lithium demand (especially from Chinese EV makers), this one stays speculative. Sit tight for now — the long-term case isn't broken, just delayed.

watch_today.title: Oil crashes 5.7% — what it means for your portfolio
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) dropped sharply to $84.25 last night — down 5.7% — as Iran ceasefire signals reduced the risk of supply disruptions. Cheaper oil is generally good for consumers and can ease inflation, which could give the RBA more room to cut rates. Broadly positive for growth-oriented holdings like VDHG and VTS.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI thematic still intact, patience required
watch_today.detail: GXAI ticked up 0.32% today and is benefiting from a broadening AI boom — CNBC reported industrials are now getting re-rated alongside tech. The fund is still down 17.9% overall, but the long-term AI thematic story is very much alive. Hold and let it ride.

watch_today.title: GOOG — strong earnings, solid hold
watch_today.detail: Alphabet just posted $119.8B in Q2 revenue and the stock nudged up last night. Motley Fool called it a buy after earnings. Your position is small but profitable (up 3.8%). Nothing to do here — the long-term case is solid and AI integration into Google Search and Cloud is accelerating.

world.summary: The US-Iran conflict dominates global headlines, with Washington pausing strikes to create space for diplomacy. Meanwhile, a major US-Brazil diplomatic standoff is escalating ahead of Brazil's elections, and US courts are pushing back hard on Trump's voter suppression efforts.

stories.title: US pauses Iran strikes as diplomacy window opens — but casualties remain disputed
stories.why_it_matters: The US has held off on fresh strikes against Iran for a second consecutive day, with the US ambassador confirming the pause is deliberate — to create space for diplomatic talks. The NYT reports that Trump held back from a major escalation after advisers raised serious concerns. Separately, 7News reported that four US troop deaths were removed from the official Iran casualty tally, adding confusion around the true human cost. The Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea have already been disrupted — and Al Jazeera now reports the conflict may be spreading toward the Caspian Sea. Oil falling sharply today (down 5.7%) suggests markets are pricing in a de-escalation, but this situation remains volatile.

stories.title: Brazil blocks Trump officials from entering the country ahead of elections
stories.why_it_matters: Brazil has denied visas to a US government delegation that was reportedly sent to cast doubt on Brazil's election system ahead of the country's upcoming national vote. Brazilian officials say the move was a direct rejection of outside interference. This is a serious diplomatic clash between the world's two largest democracies — Trump's team has previously echoed claims of election fraud in Brazil's 2022 vote. The standoff could have implications for trade relations between the US and Latin America's biggest economy.

stories.title: US courts block Trump's mail-in voting crackdown and federal voter list
stories.why_it_matters: Two separate US courts have ruled against the Trump administration this week on voting rights. A federal appeals court rejected Trump's attempt to restrict mail-in voting across 23 states, and another court upheld an injunction blocking Trump's executive order to create a centralised federal voter registration list. These rulings are significant — they suggest the judiciary is acting as a brake on executive power in the lead-up to the 2026 midterm elections. For Australians watching US democracy closely, this is a key story about institutional checks and balances holding firm.

stories.title: Iran conflict reaches the Caspian Sea — a new front opens
stories.why_it_matters: Al Jazeera is reporting that the US-Iran conflict — which has already disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea — may now be spreading to the Caspian Sea region. This matters because it would involve entirely new geographies, potentially drawing in Russia, Azerbaijan and Central Asian nations. The Caspian is a major oil and gas corridor. If instability spreads there, it could put upward pressure on energy prices again, even as markets celebrate the current pause in strikes.

markets.summary: The ASX had a cracking session today, up 1.4% to close at 8,894 — one of its best days in recent weeks. The strong day was broadly supported across sectors. Last night in the US, the S&P 500 was basically flat (+0.05%) while the NASDAQ dipped 0.64% as some tech names pulled back. The big story in markets is oil — WTI crude cratered 5.7% to $84.25 as Iran ceasefire hopes eased fears of a supply shock. Gold continues to climb, now at $4,093/oz. The Aussie dollar is at 70 US cents, its strongest level in a while.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Strong rally today — up 1.4% to close near 8,900. Broad-based gains across the market.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session was virtually flat — the US market is in wait-and-see mode ahead of major earnings this week.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The NASDAQ slipped 0.64% last night as some large-cap tech names gave back gains. Big earnings coming this week.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Massive drop — oil fell 5.7% as Iran ceasefire signals reduced supply disruption fears. Good for inflation, good for consumers.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold keeps climbing, up 0.6% to a fresh high near $4,093/oz. Investors are still hedging against uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar broke back above 70 US cents — its strongest level in some time. Helped by stronger commodity sentiment and a softer US dollar.

politics.summary: All eyes are on Wednesday's inflation data, which will be the decisive factor in the RBA's next interest rate decision. Separately, the Albanese government has a rift emerging over euthanasia telehealth policy.

stories.title: Wednesday's CPI print is 'do or die' for the RBA's next rate call
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's June quarter Consumer Price Index (CPI — basically the official measure of how fast prices are rising) lands Wednesday morning. It's being described as 'do or die' for the Reserve Bank's August meeting. If inflation is still running hot, the RBA may be forced to hike rates again — something Nine.com.au reports could push a significant number of mortgage holders to sell their homes. If the number comes in soft, a rate cut could be on the table. The RBA has also publicly complained that many Australians don't understand inflation — not a great look for a central bank asking people to trust its decisions.

stories.title: Albanese at odds with Labor over telehealth euthanasia consultations
stories.why_it_matters: The Guardian reports that Prime Minister Albanese is at odds with the ALP's own policy position on whether telehealth (remote video consultations) should be permitted for voluntary assisted dying (euthanasia) consultations. Labor's policy now says it should be allowed, but Albanese appears to disagree. This is a sensitive social policy area that could cause internal friction for the government, particularly given it intersects with both healthcare access in regional areas and personal conscience issues for MPs.

stories.title: Albanese government faces calls to resolve 'Death Tax' and 'Widows Tax' issues
stories.why_it_matters: The National Tribune is calling on Albanese to defuse several politically charged issues including what critics call a 'Death Tax' (inheritance-related tax concerns), a 'Widows Tax' (superannuation rules that can leave surviving spouses financially disadvantaged), and a so-called 'Secret Divorce' issue relating to asset splitting. These are niche but emotionally resonant issues for older Australians and retirees — groups that Labor needs to keep onside. No major policy announcements yet, but the pressure is building.

ai.summary: The dominant AI story this week is regulation — a global debate is heating up about whether to rein in AI or let it run. Meanwhile, China's Moonshot AI is releasing a major new open model, and Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro is still nowhere to be seen despite being announced months ago.

stories.title: Andrew Forrest warns: regulate AI or face 'extinction'
stories.why_it_matters: Billionaire mining magnate Andrew Forrest has issued a stark warning in the AFR, saying that failing to regulate artificial intelligence could leave humanity 'naive to extinction.' Forrest is pushing for strong government oversight of AI development, arguing the technology is advancing faster than society's ability to control it. This puts him on the opposite side of many tech industry figures who argue over-regulation will kill innovation and productivity — a debate that's going global right now.

stories.title: China's Moonshot AI to release Kimi K3 — a powerful open-source model
stories.why_it_matters: China's Moonshot AI startup is preparing to release its Kimi K3 model as a downloadable, open-source tool — meaning anyone can run it on their own hardware. This is significant because it means cutting-edge Chinese AI will be freely available globally, putting more pressure on Western models like GPT-4 and Claude. China is clearly not waiting for global AI regulation to catch up — it's racing to get its models into the hands of as many users as possible.

stories.title: Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro is still missing in action
stories.why_it_matters: Mashable is asking the obvious question: where is Gemini 3.5 Pro? Google announced the model at its big I/O conference months ago, but it still hasn't been released. Competitors like Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (ChatGPT) and xAI (Grok) have all been shipping updates regularly. For Google investors, this is worth watching — delays in flagship AI releases can signal internal development struggles and leave market share on the table.

stories.title: Global AI regulation is shifting from talk to actual enforcement
stories.why_it_matters: A new analysis from Cyprus Mail notes that global AI governance is no longer just about publishing strategy documents — regulators in Europe and beyond are now actively enforcing AI rules, issuing fines and requiring compliance. The EU's AI Act is the most advanced framework, with China pushing to play a leading role in shaping international standards. For Australian businesses and investors, this regulatory wave is coming — companies that get ahead of compliance will be better positioned than those that don't.

sport.summary: The NRL's Round 21 wrapped up with the Sharks looking dominant, the Broncos in deep trouble, and the Titans delivering a milestone-spoiling win over the Dragons. AFL news includes a major State of Origin format shake-up being flagged, Brisbane Lions keeping finals hopes alive, and a suspension verdict on a young gun.

stories.title: Sharks perfect 10 — Manly mauled in Round 21
stories.why_it_matters: Cronulla had a near-perfect Round 21, thrashing Manly in what ABC News described as a 'perfect 10' performance. The Sea Eagles (who are on a bye in Round 22) will be stinging from this one. Sharks are building serious form heading into the back half of the season.

stories.title: Broncos season on life support after Cowboys loss
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports describes the Broncos' season as being on 'life support' after another loss to the Cowboys. Brisbane face the Knights at Suncorp Stadium on Saturday night in Round 22 — a must-win game. Fox Sports called it the 'story of their season,' pointing to a consistent inability to close out games when it matters.

stories.title: Titans spoil Gutho's milestone and expose Dragons' concerns
stories.why_it_matters: The Gold Coast Titans beat the Dragons, spoiling what was meant to be a milestone celebration for Clint Gutherson. Fox Sports flagged a 'major concern' for the Dragons heading into Round 22 where they face the Dolphins. The Titans face the Warriors at Cbus Super Stadium on Saturday — a big local game for Gold Coast fans.

stories.title: AFL boss flags major State of Origin format changes
stories.why_it_matters: AFL CEO Andrew Dillon has flagged that the AFL State of Origin concept could undergo significant format changes. The AFL's own site reports Dillon saying 'we'll work through that,' hinting at potential expansion or restructuring. Zero Hanger notes the AFL boss is open to big changes, which could shake up the interstate rivalry format that's been gaining traction. No firm details yet, but it's clearly being seriously considered at the top level.

stories.title: Brisbane Lions keep finals push alive with late win over Port Adelaide
stories.why_it_matters: The Brisbane Lions unleashed a 'late avalanche' to beat Port Adelaide and keep themselves within striking distance of the top two on the AFL ladder. The result keeps Brisbane's finals push very much alive heading into the back end of the home-and-away season. Port Adelaide will be disappointed to give up a lead late.
